summary.title: The Different CTO Roles
summary.one_liner: Learn the four common CTO role models (Infrastructure Manager, Technology Visionary and Operations Manager, External Facing Technologist, Big Thinker) and how their scope and influence differ.
keywords: role of a cto in corporate innovation
takeaways: The CTO role has no single definition; it varies with company type and how central technology is to the business.
Tom Berray's four-quadrant model classifies CTOs as Infrastructure Manager, Technology Visionary and Operations Manager, External Facing Technologist, or Big Thinker.

In the first two models the CTO manages an engineering division and influences through internal technology development; in the last two the CTO must influence other divisions and often reports to the CEO.
The first CTOs appeared in the late 1980s when R&D lab directors were moved into roles using technology for strategic advantage.
The post lists further sources, including Aspatore's Leading CTOs, Mark Minevich's The CTO Handbook, and Roger Smith's writings on CTO patterns.
summary.summary: Werner Vogels, Amazon's CTO, explains why the CTO role is poorly defined and how it changes with company type. He traces the role's origins to the late 1980s and presents Tom Berray's four-quadrant framework: Infrastructure Manager, Technology Visionary and Operations Manager, External Facing Technologist, and Big Thinker. Each model is described by its typical responsibilities and how the CTO exerts influence, with the first two managing engineering divisions and the last two relying on executive-level influence. The post ends with a list of reading sources for further research.
